description: This data set records indoor temperatures in the Maternity and Gynaecology building of the Royal Berkshire Hospital in Reading, England, during the hot summer of 2018, to understand why its rooms overheat. The producers are Hannah Gough, Zhiwen Luo and Samuel Faulknall-Mills at the University of Reading, working with the hospital as a pilot to improve patient safety. Coverage is one floor of one hospital building over two months, July and August 2018, in conditions just short of a heatwave. Nine Tinytag temperature and humidity loggers placed at floor and desk level in scanning rooms, offices and other spaces logged every five minutes; they were inter-calibrated and the data are kept as they came off the instruments. The files are available as a free download from the University of Reading Research Data Archive under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, and the analysis is published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. Caveats: a single building and summer, no outdoor or energy data in this description, and the archive page timed out from this environment, so file formats were not checked. Simulation uses: validating building thermal models of hospitals, testing cooling and shading measures for heat adaptation, and quantifying how heatwaves reduce usable clinical space. Related records: the Caribbean smart hospitals case (case_study-caribbean-smart-hospitals) covers climate retrofits of health facilities.
